            It is disabled only while that conversation has nothing to carry
            on and no run in it is under way, its tooltip then saying the next
            task, or question, already starts a new conversation.

            Both sit on the bar's bottom line, which runs beneath them as it does
            beneath the help text, and neither is cut off: the help text gives
            way to them when the bar is narrow.

        usage:
            same colour, and the line fades with the half it borders, never
            staying solid across a faded button.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode's system
        prompt is sent with it, as the @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says.

    ask:
        Ask is for simply asking a question, which runs as the
        @{PromptModesScope} says. Any number of questions can be asked, and they
        all run at the same time; asking another never stops or waits for one
        already running.

        Each question's progress and results are shown in a @{TaskTableScope}.
        The questions stack directly above the tabs, the newest nearest them, in
        a column that pushes the message list up to make room rather than
        covering it, so none of a running task's progress is ever hidden behind
        them. Each slides up out of the chat input with an animation as it is
        asked, the message list giving way above it. While the harness works on
        a question, it is a single row showing the latest thing the harness did.
        A finished question is a row with its status and first line.

        However many questions are asked, the stack is only as tall as its
        rows, up to 240 pixels, the queue's most, and scrolls beyond that with
        a @{ScrollbarScope}, kept on the newest question, nearest the tabs, as
        each is asked. Once it holds more than fit, the stack lays out only
        the rows in view, as a table does, so a long stack costs no more to show, scroll, or animate than a
        short one, and the drawer's bottom follows the stack's top as ever.

        Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status
        and first line, above its full task table, in the @{AnswerDrawerScope},
        which it fills, the table scrolling once it is taller, with its lock to
        the bottom off to start with. Only one question is open at a time:
        opening another closes the one open back down to its row. An open
        question leaves the stack for the drawer. Clicking an open question's
        heading closes it down to its row in the stack, and clicking a finished
        question's row opens it again. Each question has a close button, which
        removes it and stops it if it is still running, leaving the others
        running. A closed question becomes a previous answer.

    answerSteps:
        For a question, only the answer matters, so wherever a finished
        question's task table is shown, an open question and a previous answer,
        the table collapses the steps leading up to the answer, as the
        @{TaskTableScope} says. A question closed into the previous answers
        starts collapsed again. Tasks are never collapsed like this: see the
        @{MessageList}.

    previousAnswers:
        Previous answers are a @{HistoryListScope}, shown only while the Ask tab
        is selected, at the top of the questions stacked above the tabs. It
        lists every question asked before and closed: those saved with the
        project and those closed since. Its row reads "No previous answers",
        "1 previous answer", or "N previous answers", and while expanded,
        "Back to the questions". Each previous answer offers Resend, which asks
        its question again, as the @{PromptSendingScope} says. Expanded, the
        row and the list go into the @{AnswerDrawerScope}, sliding up from on
        top of any question rows still in the stack. The questions asked from
        now on carry on the conversation the latest of them left off.

    answerDrawer: @{AnswerDrawerScope}

    selectingAnswerText:
        The text of an answer being viewed, in the answer drawer, whether an
        open question or a previous answer, can be selected by dragging across
        it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the drawer
        shows a @{SelectionPopoverScope} with two buttons: "Copy", with a copy
        icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon.

        Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard. Attach to prompt adds it
        to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the selection. The
        popover also closes when the drawer closes.

    attachments:
        What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between
        the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were
        attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece
        of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an
        ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it
        has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose
        tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.

        Images can be attached too: pasted from the clipboard while the chat
        input has focus, dropped onto the chat input from the file manager, or
        chosen with a small ghost button with an image icon, whose tooltip says
        "Attach images", on the tab row between the last tab and the help
        text, which opens the platform's file picker for any files, several at
        once, since the picker can't be limited to images. Pasting an image
        attaches it rather than putting anything in the text, even when the
        clipboard holds text as well; every image on the clipboard is
        attached, and a clipboard with no image pastes its text as usual.
        Several files dropped or chosen at once are attached in their order,
        each on its own merits. An image is known by its content, not
        its name, and only PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP are taken: anything else
        pasted, dropped, or chosen, BMP, TIFF, and SVG included, is not
        attached, and a warning notification titled "Not attached" says it
        isn't an image. An image larger than 5 MB is not attached either, and
        the same notification says it is too large. A folder dropped or chosen
        isn't an image either, and a file that can't be read is not attached,
        the same notification saying it couldn't be read, and why. Each file
        left out has its own notification, and the others are still attached.

        Files can be dropped only on the chat input itself, its tabs, the
        attachments, and the text input; dropping them on the message list
        above it does nothing. While files are dragged over the chat input,
        its background is highlighted with the accent's fill, laid about a
        quarter of the way over it.

        An attached
        image's row shows a small thumbnail, its file name, or "Pasted image"
        for one pasted, and its size in pixels, muted, with the same remove
        button; hovering the thumbnail shows the image larger, at most 320
        pixels. Images and text are listed together in the order they were
        attached while the prompt is written. A prompt taken back into the
        input, as when a queued prompt is edited, lists its text first, then
        its images, each image named by its saved file, a pasted one
        included.

        Attachments belong to the prompt being written, not to a tab: switching
        tabs keeps them all, and they go with the prompt whichever tab it is
        sent from. When the prompt is sent, its attachments are sent along with
        it and the list empties, as the text input does. A queued prompt keeps
        the attachments it was sent with.

    projects:
        The questions stacked above the tabs, the open answer, and the previous
        answers belong to their project, as the @{OpenProjectsScope} says:
        switching projects shows those of the project switched to, while the
        questions of other projects carry on running in the background. The
        prompt being written, its attachments, the selected tab, and the Slice
        toggle stay as they are across a switch, and are sent to the project on screen.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) brings it back, from
        anywhere the chat input isn't beneath something else, as the
        @{MainWindowScope} says.

    growToFit:
        The text input is a @{GrowingTextInputScope} growing to 12 rows at most.
        Its first row lines up with the send button, both at the top of the
        input row, and it grows downward from there.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

use /lib
use /ui
use /ui/components/sidebar/Sidebar
from ./referenced-files import ReferencedFilesPanel
from ./subagents import SubagentsPanel
from ./understanding import UnderstandingPanel
from /scope/application/Body import BodyScope
from /ui/components/scrollbar import ScrollbarScope
from /ui/components/sidebar import SidebarScope

export sidebar RightSidebarScope:
    side: right

    panels:
        - @{ReferencedFilesPanel}
        - @{UnderstandingPanel}
        - @{SubagentsPanel}

    concept: {RightSidebarConcept}

concept RightSidebarConcept:
    pitch:
        A second @{SidebarScope}, at the right of the message list and the
        chat input beneath it, that lists
        the spec files the running task references, so it's clear what part of
        the spec the harness is working from, and the constraints it has taken
        from it for the task.

    shape: {RightSidebarShape}

shape RightSidebarShape:
    description:
        It runs the full height of the body, beside the body's tab bar, the
        message list or file beneath it, and the chat input beneath those, which stops at its left edge rather than
        running beneath it. It keeps the width it was dragged to while the
        application runs.

        Its panels sit one above the other, in this order: the referenced
        files at the top, the understanding beneath them, and the subagents
        last, along the bottom of the sidebar, beneath both. The referenced
        files are only as tall as their rows need, up to half the sidebar's
        height, scrolling beyond that; the subagents, once there are any, are
        only as tall as their rows need, up to 30% of the sidebar's height;
        and the understanding fills what is left between them, until they are
        resized. While the run has started no subagent, the understanding
        reaches the sidebar's bottom.

    resizingPanels:

        - a question closes the answer drawer and any inset panel, so its row is in view
        - a divergence analysis, a rescope search, or a run target brings its @{MinimizablePanelScope} back
        - a spec build has nothing to show, so its row only closes the list

        with its own work, which carries on running there and is shown live as
        soon as that project is on screen again.

    belongsToAProject:
        What a project's work is, kept apart for each open project:
        - its tasks, from the @{PromptEditor}: the latest task and its output, the previous tasks, whether the harness is working on one, and the conversation tasks carry on
        - its queue, whether it is expanded, and its auto-send switch
        - its questions, from the @{ChatInputScope}'s Ask tab: those stacked above the tabs, the one open in the answer drawer, the previous answers, and the conversation questions carry on
        - a spec build run on its own in it
        - a divergence analysis, a rescope search, or a run target of it, each in its minimizable panel

        Whatever a run does is written to the project it was started in, never
        to the one on screen. A project's queue only ever sends into that
        project, and sends on its own there while it is in the background, just
        as it would on screen.

    keptAsLeft:
        Each open project also keeps how it was left on screen, so switching
        back to it shows it just as it was, with nothing to find again:
        - the message list: how far the latest task's output was scrolled and whether it was locked to the bottom, how far its compiled prompt was scrolled, the previous tasks, whether they were expanded, which was open, which were selected, and how far they were scrolled, the queue's scrolling, and the question rows' scrolling
        - the files open in the body's tabs, in their order, which tab is selected, and each file's unsaved changes, its cursor, and its scrolling
        - the file tree's expanded folders, and the row selected
        - the Git panel's commit message, as far as it was written
        - its minimizable panels, a divergence analysis, a rescope search, or the Run panel, minimized as it is switched away from, their work carrying on in the background

        Coming back to a project slides nothing in: its tabs show as they
        were, the same one selected, and its right sidebar is
        already out if a task of it is running. All of this is kept for as long as the application
        runs, and none of it is saved with the project.

    followsTheScreen:
        Only what isn't a project's follows the project on screen: the
        palette and any inset panel other than a minimizable one close, the
        language server is the project on screen's, and the settings show the
        project on screen's prompts. A file kept for a project not on screen
        isn't open in the language server, and is opened in it again once its
        project is back. The chat input's prompt being written, its
        attachments, the selected tab, and the Slice toggle stay with the
        person writing rather than a project. What the application keeps for
        the whole run rather than a project, such as the sidebar's width, the
        answer drawer's height, and which ribbon tabs are open, stays as it is.

    switching:
        A project's history, answers, and queue are loaded from its data, as the
        @{ProjectDataScope} says, the first time it is opened in a launch, and
        kept from then on, so switching back to it loads nothing again and
        @{ChatInputScope} doesn't have the keyboard, such as in an
        @{EditorScope}, the @{FileTreeScope}, or the Git panel, moves focus to it,
        with its cursor where it was, and sends nothing. While it has the
        keyboard, it sends as the chat input says. Wherever else it already
        means something, it keeps that meaning: in the palette, in a dialog,
        in the list of recent projects, and in an inset panel, which the chat
        input is beneath.

    pointer:
        Where the hit areas of two things that take a press overlap, such as
        the edge a sidebar, split, or drawer is resized by and the scrollbar of
        the list beside it, a press goes to the one with the smaller hit area,
        and only to it: a scrollbar's button, or its thumb, takes a press over
        the wider strip of a resize edge, while the edge takes one over the
        scrollbar's track when the edge is the smaller. The cursor shows what a
        press there would do.
        @{ProjectSidebarScope}, which runs the full height beside it, and
        reaching the window's right edge. It is part of the @{PromptEditor}.

        The @{ChatInputScope} lives within the body, along its bottom: its
        left edge against the project sidebar, and above it, beneath the
        body's tab bar, the selected tab's contents: the message list, or an
        open file. While a task runs, the @{RightSidebarScope} runs
        the body's full height at its right, beside the tab bar, the selected
        tab's contents, and the chat input, and the chat input's right edge is against it: the chat input
        never runs beneath the right sidebar. While that sidebar isn't there,
        the chat input reaches the window's right edge.

        The body is flat and quiet: the selected tab's contents, the message
        list or an open file, sit on the theme's base surface, #444444 in dark
        mode, running edge to edge with no border, and the chat input along

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/application/Body import BodyScope
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/open-projects import OpenProjectsScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/modes import PromptModesScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/sending import PromptSendingScope
from /ui/components/scrollbar import ScrollbarScope
from /ui/components/selection-popover import SelectionPopoverScope
from /ui/components/task-table import TaskTableScope
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope

export ui-component AskConversationScope:
    concept: {AskConversationConcept}

concept AskConversationConcept:
    pitch:
        The questions asked from the Ask tab, read as a chat: every question
        and its answer, one after another, in a pane of its own beside the
        tasks, with each new conversation clearly marked where it begins.

    shape: {AskConversationShape}

shape AskConversationShape:
    description:
        While the @{ChatInputScope}'s Ask tab is selected, the
        @{BodyScope} splits in two, side by side, above the chat input: the
        body's tab bar and the selected tab's contents on the left, and this
        pane on the right. It goes when another tab is selected, the left
        side taking the body's full width again, and comes back as it was,
        scrolled where it was, when Ask is selected again. Nothing slides as
        it comes and goes.

        It is drawn in the @{ThemeScope}'s roles, on the same base surface as
        the selected tab's contents beside it, with the theme's line between
        the two halves. Along its top runs a header as tall as the body's tab
        bar, 32 pixels, on the tab bar's background with the theme's line
        beneath it, reading "Questions" at its left, with 12 pixels of
        padding, and at its right how many questions it holds, muted.

    split:
        The pane starts at half the width of the space it shares with the
        left side. The line between them is a resize edge: hovering it shows
        the resize cursor for left and right and a thin line in the theme's
        accent, and dragging it moves it, following the pointer exactly, from
        25% to 75% of that space, both sides laid out anew at each width. The
        width it is dragged to is kept for as long as the application runs,
        for every project, and none of it is saved.

    conversation:
        The pane lists every question of the project, those saved with it
        and those asked since, running or finished, oldest at the top and the
        newest at the bottom, the way a chat reads. Each is a message and its
        reply. The question is shown as it was typed, not as it was compiled,
        in a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted Ask's colour,
        as the @{PromptModesScope} colours it, with corners rounded 6 pixels,
        set against the pane's right edge and at most 80% of its width,
        wrapping within that, with anything it was sent with, attached text
        and images, listed beneath its text as the chat input lists them.
        Beneath the box, at its right, sits a small muted line with the time
        it was asked and, once it is finished, a Resend button, which asks the
        question again as the @{PromptSendingScope} says, the new question
        coming in at the bottom.

        Its answer follows beneath it, against the pane's left edge and the
        pane's full width, with no box: its @{TaskTableScope}, collapsing the
        steps leading up to the answer as the table says, so what is read is
        the answer. While the harness works on it, the table grows as the
        harness does, beneath a status line with a spinner and the latest
        thing the harness did, and a Stop button at the status line's right
        stops just that question, leaving the others running. A question that
        failed or was stopped shows its status in the table as any task
        does. Questions are 16 pixels apart, and a question's answer 8 pixels
        beneath it.

        Questions asked while another is still running come in at the bottom
        in the order they were asked, each answered in its own place as its
        harness goes, so answers can be filling in at once.

    newConversation:
        Where a new conversation begins, it is clearly marked: above the first
        question of each conversation, the first question in the pane
        included, runs a divider across the pane's full width, a line in Ask's
        colour at either side of a label reading "New conversation", then,
        muted, the date and time its first question was asked. A question
        starts a new conversation as its saved record says, in its hidden
        anchor's newConversation, as the @{ChatInputScope} says; a question
        saved before that was recorded carries on the one above it, unless it
        is the first. A question asked while another was running carries on a
        copy of that conversation, as the @{HarnessIntegrationScope} says, and
        is not marked.

        Pressing New conversation for questions puts the divider in at the
        bottom of the pane straight away, beneath the last question, reading
        "New conversation" with no time, so it is plain that the next
        question starts with no context; the time is filled in once that
        question is asked. Pressed again with nothing asked since, it adds no
        second divider.

    scrolling:
        The pane scrolls, with a @{ScrollbarScope}, and opens scrolled to the
        bottom, on the newest question, the first time it is shown. While it
        is at the bottom it stays locked there, following each question asked
        and each answer as it grows; scrolling up unlocks it, and scrolling
        back to the bottom locks it again. Asking a question always scrolls it
        to the bottom and locks it. However many questions it holds, and
        however long their answers, it lays out only what is in view: each
        question, divider, and row of an answer's table is drawn as it
        scrolls into view, so a long conversation costs no more to show,
        scroll, or resize than a short one.

    empty:
        With no question asked yet, the pane reads "No questions yet. Ask one
        below.", muted, centred in it.

    selectingText:
        The text of any question or answer in the pane can be selected by
        dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending
        within the pane shows a @{SelectionPopoverScope} with two buttons:
        "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip
        icon. Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard; Attach to prompt
        adds it to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the
        selection, and the popover closes when the pane goes.

    elsewhere:
        While another tab is selected, the questions still running stay in
        view as small rows stacked directly above the chat input's tabs, the
        newest nearest them, each showing its first line and the latest thing
        the harness did, in a column that pushes what is above it up rather
        than covering it, up to 240 pixels tall and scrolling beyond that. A
        question leaves the stack once it finishes. Clicking one selects the
        Ask tab, the pane scrolled to that question. There is no stack while
        Ask is selected: its questions are in the pane.

    projects:
        The pane shows the questions of the project on screen, as the
        @{OpenProjectsScope} says, and each project keeps how far its pane was
        scrolled and whether it was locked to the bottom while the
        application runs; questions of other projects carry on running in the
        background.

content.text:
I've changed the spec so that in Ask mode the body splits and the question history shows beside the tasks as a chat, with a clear marker where each new conversation starts. I haven't touched `src/`. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton format --check` passes, and `piton build` wrote 75 files and removed the old answer-drawer reference page. `piton reach` shows the new pane is reached from the entry.

A few choices here are mine, not yours — tell me if any should change:
- **Side by side.** The Ask history goes on the right, the tab bar and message list or file stay on the left, and the chat input still runs along the bottom beneath both.
- **Replace, don't add.** The history list, the pop-up answer panel and the stack of question rows are replaced by the new pane rather than kept alongside it. The per-question close button is gone too; a running question has a Stop button instead.
- **Chat look.** Each question sits in a lightly green-tinted box on the right, and its answer runs full width beneath it with no box.
- **Other tabs.** Questions still running show as small rows above the chat input's tabs. Clicking one switches to Ask and scrolls to it.

## What changed in the spec

**New: `AskConversationScope`** (`spec/scope/prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.pi`)
- **When it shows:** only while the Ask tab is selected, as a pane on the right of the body, above the chat input. It has a 32-pixel header reading "Questions" with a muted count.
- **Resizing:** it starts at half the width. The edge between the two sides drags from 25% to 75%, and the width is kept for as long as the app runs.
- **Chat layout:** every question in the project, oldest at the top. Each question is shown as typed, with a time line and a Resend button once finished. Its answer is the task table, with the steps leading up to the answer collapsed. A running question shows a spinner, the latest step and a Stop button.
- **New conversation marker:** a full-width divider in the Ask colour reading "New conversation" and the start time. It goes above the first question of each conversation, based on the `newConversation` flag saved with the question. Questions that carry on a copy of a running question's conversation aren't marked.
  - Pressing New conversation adds a divider with no time at the bottom straight away; the time fills in when the next question is asked. Pressing it again with nothing asked since adds no second divider.
- **Scrolling:** it opens at the bottom and stays there while you're at the bottom. Scrolling up releases it, and asking a question jumps back down. Only what's in view is laid out.
- **Also:**
  - Empty state: "No questions yet. Ask one below."
  - Selecting text shows Copy and Attach to prompt.
  - Each project keeps its own scroll position.

**Edited:**
- `BodyScope`:
  - new `askSplit` property;
  - `contents` lists the pane;
  - `tabs` says the tab bar ends at the split while it's shown;
  - `sliding` moves the pane with the right sidebar;
  - `openFile` wording updated.
- `ChatInputShape`: `ask` and `answerSteps` rewritten; `previousAnswers`, `answerDrawer` and `selectingAnswerText` removed; `askConversation` added; `projects` and the two attachment sections updated; unused imports dropped.
- `PromptEditorShape`: `history` now says questions come back in the pane and are saved when stopped; mentions of previous answers removed from `previousTasks`, `previousTaskFilters` and `rawPrompt`.
- Wording updated to match in `HistoryListScope`, the running-activity list (a question row now switches to Ask and scrolls to it), and `OpenProjectsScope`.

**Deleted:** `AnswerDrawerScope` and `MessageListAskDimmingShape`, along with the `askDimming` entry in `MessageList`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `AskConversationScope` and all its shape properties (`split`, `conversation`, `newConversation`, `scrolling`, `empty`, `selectingText`, `elsewhere`, `projects`)
- `BodyShape.askSplit`, `.contents`, `.tabs`, `.sliding`, `.openFile`
- `ChatInputShape.ask`, `.answerSteps`, `.askConversation`, `.projects`
- `PromptEditorShape.history`
- `OpenProjectsScope` (`belongsToAProject`, `keptAsLeft`, `followsTheScreen`) and the running-activity `list`

The code should remove the answer drawer, its dimming, and the previous answers list and its expanded state. It should also stop showing finished questions in the stack above the tabs.
